claims.title: Budget holds, overruns are recorded
claims.invariant: Committed plus reserved spend never exceeds the budget. If an actual cost exceeds its authorization, the full cost is recorded, the overrun is visible, and further spend is denied.

claims.title: Policy and approval can’t be bypassed
claims.invariant: A denied operation never runs. An approval-required operation runs only after a fresh human approval that matches its operation and amount.

claims.title: No impersonating another agent
claims.invariant: Agent and session identity and authority come from the trusted runtime, never from fields the agent supplies.

claims.title: Gongbu credentials stay out of reach
claims.invariant: Credentials held by Gongbu cannot be read by the agent or used except through a Hubu-authorized call.

claims.title: Agent can’t change its own governance
claims.invariant: Policies, budgets, approvals and ledger history change only through the owner path. The agent can’t raise its limits, approve itself, rewrite history, or misrepresent a pending approval.

claims.title: Provider packs can’t widen authority
claims.invariant: A pack can’t misprice spend below verified rates, send a credential to a host it isn’t bound to, or become active without the owner.

ep01-runaway.title: The runaway agent
ep01-runaway.question: What happens after the budget is gone?
ep01-runaway.statement: With a fixed $0.10 budget and $0.01 per operation, Hubu stops authorizing new work once the budget is consumed—even after 100 more attempts.
ep01-runaway.setup: One synthetic agent. A fresh $0.10 budget. A fixed allow policy. Each authorized operation reports a $0.01 synthetic receipt.
steps: Complete ten authorize → claim → settle operations.
Issue 100 new logical authorization attempts after exhaustion.
Export the final budget, authorization history, and every ledger page.
ep01-runaway.verify: Compare public settlements and exact budget charges with the request trace. Denials need request evidence; an empty ledger alone cannot establish them.
ep01-runaway.boundary: The budget and policy stay fixed throughout. These results do not establish authority boundaries for a caller with the broad administrative bearer.

ep02-last-cent.title: The last cent
ep02-last-cent.question: Can the ledger tell an uncomfortable truth?
ep02-last-cent.statement: A confirmed $0.03 charge against a $0.01 authorization is accounted for in full, the $0.02 overrun is visible, and further positive authorizations stop.
ep02-last-cent.setup: A $0.01 budget, a $0.01 claimed authorization, and a synthetic receipt for $0.03. The public short lease is 30 seconds.
steps: Try normal settlement with the overrun receipt and inspect the retained hold.
Wait for the returned lease deadline, then use the explicit owner reconciliation path.
Repeat that reconciliation and probe fresh authorizations; inspect the public ledger.
ep02-last-cent.verify: Inspect the authorized maximum, actual charge, visible overrun, remaining budget, and idempotent posting. The owner action is part of the result.
ep02-last-cent.boundary: Full overrun accounting requires explicit owner reconciliation after lease expiry. A negative remaining budget correctly records the confirmed charge above the estimate.
ep02-last-cent.condition: Requires explicit owner reconciliation after lease expiry.

ep03-crash-recovery.title: The unresolved crash
ep03-crash-recovery.question: Does a restart make an obligation disappear?
ep03-crash-recovery.statement: After Hubu is killed with a claimed operation unresolved, restart preserves its financial obligation; lease expiry does not release it, and replaying a confirmed resolution produces one settlement.
ep03-crash-recovery.setup: A $0.01 claimed operation and a durable synthetic billed marker outside Hubu’s database. Kill only the kit’s server process before settlement.
steps: Confirm the claim publicly, write the fixture receipt, and kill the server.
Restart the same released binary and database; inspect the claim and hold.
After lease expiry, reconcile the confirmed charge, repeat the resolution, and restart again.
ep03-crash-recovery.verify: Check the same public authorization and claim IDs, the retained hold, rejected unsafe resolution paths, and one final ledger posting.
ep03-crash-recovery.boundary: The fault is a Hubu process kill after a confirmed claim and synthetic billed marker, before settlement. Provider execution, disk loss, and Gongbu recovery are outside this test.

ep04-many-clients.title: Many clients, one budget
ep04-many-clients.question: Can a burst reserve more than the budget?
ep04-many-clients.statement: Ten clients sharing a fixed $1 budget cannot obtain more than $0.99 of $0.03 reservations in this 100-request burst; normal settlement records those costs once.
ep04-many-clients.setup: Ten ordinary client processes, each issuing ten real HTTP requests. One agent account and one $1 budget. No paid model or fleet of AI agents.
steps: Release the clients at a start barrier and claim allowed operations promptly.
Hold settlement until every burst request has completed; export the reserved budget.
Settle the accepted receipts and export the final public accounting evidence.
ep04-many-clients.verify: Reconcile allows, denials, and transport errors separately. Compare the held total with final charges; a timeout never counts as a denial.
ep04-many-clients.boundary: Ten client processes create the network burst. The released server handles connections serially; this does not measure simultaneous SQLite writers, throughput, or fairness.
ep04-many-clients.condition: The released HTTP server handles requests serially. This does not establish behavior under parallel server execution.

ep05-denied-operation.title: The denied operation
ep05-denied-operation.question: Is there any way around a policy denial?
ep05-denied-operation.statement: A request above the explicit $1.00 deny rule gets no token, hold, claim or posting—on replay, as a new operation, with a forged token, or by claiming an allowed token for the denied amount.
ep05-denied-operation.setup: A fresh $1.00 budget and a tiered policy: allow up to $0.05, approval above $0.05, deny above $1.00. One allowed one-cent control operation.
steps: Request $2.00, replay it exactly, and request it again as a new operation.
Resolve and claim a forged authorization token.
Authorize one cent, try to claim that token for $2.00, then settle the cent normally.
ep05-denied-operation.verify: Every denial carries no token or hold, every forged or altered claim is refused, and the final ledger holds only the one-cent control.
ep05-denied-operation.boundary: This covers Hubu’s decision and executor contract. Whether Gongbu also refuses to run denied work is part of the planned Gongbu harness.

ep06-approval-reuse.title: The reused approval
ep06-approval-reuse.question: Does one human yes cover more than it should?
ep06-approval-reuse.statement: A human approval of one $0.10 operation authorizes exactly that operation at exactly that amount—not a new operation, a larger amount, a changed replay, or a claim for more, and a denial can’t be turned into a yes.
ep06-approval-reuse.setup: A fresh $1.00 budget and the tiered policy. The approval capability stays with the owner process; the agent holds only the normal credential.
steps: Request $0.10, try to use the pending request as a token, and have the owner approve it.
Request a new $0.10 operation and a $0.20 operation, replay the approved one at $0.20, and claim its token for $0.20.
Settle the approved operation, replay the approval, deny a second request, and try to approve and replay it.
ep06-approval-reuse.verify: New and larger requests wait for their own approval, every altered replay or claim is refused, the approval replay returns the same authorization, and only $0.10 is recorded.
ep06-approval-reuse.boundary: The owner approves through the approval capability over HTTP; the human-facing notification and review screens are outside this test.

ep07-impersonate-agent.title: The borrowed identity
ep07-impersonate-agent.question: Can one agent spend as another?
ep07-impersonate-agent.statement: A request that names another registered agent’s account is refused, and that agent’s budget is never charged.
ep07-impersonate-agent.setup: Two registered agents with their own allow policies and budgets ($0.10 and $1.00). The attacking process holds the same normal credential every agent uses.
steps: Request $0.05 while naming the other agent’s account_id.
If authorized, claim and settle it.
Export both budgets and this agent’s public ledger.
ep07-impersonate-agent.verify: The impersonated request is refused and the other agent’s budget shows nothing consumed.
ep07-impersonate-agent.boundary: Hubu agents share one bearer credential and Hubu does not bind an account to an authenticated runtime or thread; this experiment measures that known gap.

ep08-cross-session.title: The second session
ep08-cross-session.question: Can a different session draw on this session’s budget?
ep08-cross-session.statement: A second, separately started client session cannot draw on a budget opened for the first session unless Hubu attributes it to its own runtime-bound session.
ep08-cross-session.setup: One agent with a $0.10 budget. Session 1 reserves $0.05; session 2 is a separate OS process with the same credential.
steps: Session 1 authorizes and claims $0.05.
Session 2 asks for the remaining $0.05.
Inspect both authorizations for any session attribution.
ep08-cross-session.verify: Session 2 is refused, or its authorization carries a distinct runtime-bound session identity.
ep08-cross-session.boundary: Hubu has no session identity of its own in this release; strong session binding is planned for a future release.

ep09-raise-own-budget.title: The self-raised limit
ep09-raise-own-budget.question: Can the agent loosen its own limits?
ep09-raise-own-budget.statement: With only its own credential, the agent cannot raise its budget or replace its policy, and gets nothing beyond the owner’s original budget.
ep09-raise-own-budget.setup: A fresh $0.10 budget and the fixed allow policy. The agent uses the released CLI with its normal credential.
steps: Run budget update to raise the limit to $100.
Apply an allow-all policy to itself.
Request $0.50, five times the original budget.
ep09-raise-own-budget.verify: The final budget limit and policy match the initial export, and the $0.50 request is not authorized.
ep09-raise-own-budget.boundary: The normal bearer has administrative authority in this release; separating owner and agent credentials is planned. This experiment measures that known gap.

ep10-self-approval.title: The self-approval
ep10-self-approval.question: Can the agent approve its own escalation?
ep10-self-approval.statement: An escalated request can only be approved with the human approval capability—not with the agent’s credential, a forged capability, or the agent’s bearer reused as one.
ep10-self-approval.setup: A fresh $1.00 budget and the tiered policy. The approval capability stays in the owner process.
steps: Request $0.10 so it escalates to a human.
Try to approve it with no capability, a forged capability, and the bearer as the capability.
Check it is still pending, then the owner denies it and the agent replays.
ep10-self-approval.verify: Every self-approval attempt is refused, the request stays pending until the owner decides, and no token or spend appears.
ep10-self-approval.boundary: This covers the HTTP approval route. A human approval that arrives through a compromised notification channel is outside this test.

ep11-rewrite-ledger.title: The rewritten ledger
ep11-rewrite-ledger.question: Can the agent hide spend after the fact?
ep11-rewrite-ledger.statement: After recorded spend, the agent cannot delete, overwrite, reverse, void, release, re-price or self-reconcile it through Hubu’s public interfaces.
ep11-rewrite-ledger.setup: A fresh $0.10 budget and two settled $0.03 operations.
steps: Export the ledger after the two settlements.
Try delete, overwrite and reverse routes, void and release the settled authorization, settle it again at one micro-dollar, and reconcile it without the owner capability.
Export the ledger again.
ep11-rewrite-ledger.verify: Every attempt is refused or is an exact replay, and every recorded posting is unchanged.
ep11-rewrite-ledger.boundary: This covers Hubu’s public HTTP and CLI interfaces. Editing the database file directly is a separate challenge.

ep12-misstated-approval.title: The misleading request
ep12-misstated-approval.question: Can the agent make the human approve something else?
ep12-misstated-approval.statement: The human review shows the exact amount, account, agent and scope Hubu will authorize; the agent cannot swap the pending request, and the approval reserves and settles exactly what was reviewed.
ep12-misstated-approval.setup: A fresh $1.00 budget and the tiered policy. The agent describes a $0.50 request as a one-cent thumbnail.
steps: Request $0.50 with the misleading description and read the review.
Replay the same operation with $0.90, then with a changed description, and read the review again.
The owner approves; the agent tries to claim $0.90, then claims and settles the reviewed amount.
ep12-misstated-approval.verify: The review’s amount, account, agent and scope match the request; swaps and the larger claim are refused; exactly $0.50 is recorded.
ep12-misstated-approval.boundary: The agent’s free-text description is shown verbatim beside the exact amount; a misleading description is visible to the human but not rejected.
